name: Salvage System
description: Turns an unwanted gear instance into configured crafting materials instead of selling or deleting it. A salvage rule reads the base item, rarity and rolled affixes to determine the material grant, so a rare item can return more than a common without the bag knowing anything about gear quality. The operation is atomic at the contract level: emit inventory.itemSalvaged to remove exactly one eligible carried instance, then inventory.itemGranted for the resulting materials; rejection emits neither. Equipped, locked, quest-marked or unknown items are refused by default, preventing an inventory cleanup from silently destroying a build or objective. This component owns the conversion recipe only — the bag owns removal and storage, crafting owns later material use, and presentation owns confirmation UI.

inputs.name: salvageRules
inputs.description: Material grants by base item, rarity tier or affix tag. Rules are data, evaluated against one item instance.

inputs.name: allowEquipped
inputs.description: Whether worn items may be salvaged. False protects the current build and avoids an implicit unequip operation.

inputs.name: allowLocked
inputs.description: Whether favorited or lock-marked items may be salvaged. False requires an explicit unlock before conversion.

inputs.name: allowQuestItems
inputs.description: Whether objective-marked items may be destroyed. False keeps progression items out of the salvage stream.

outputs.name: lastSalvage
outputs.description: Source item instance, evaluated rule and granted materials, or the rejection reason.

outputs.name: itemsSalvaged
outputs.description: Successful conversions, used to audit that each removal has exactly one corresponding material grant.

provenance: Added 2026-11-02 for the Diablo loot-and-inventory extraction. Searched item sinks first: inventory.inventory_combine combines carried inputs into another item, economy.shop buys and sells for currency, inventory.crafting_bench spends materials on recipes, and inventory.slotted_bag only stores or drops items. None converts one rolled gear instance back into rarity-sensitive materials. Library-native; this is an item sink, not a crafting bench, shop or inventory owner.
